segments.sells: New Tesla cars (Model 3, Model Y, Cybertruck, Cybercab; Model S and X production ended in 2026) sold outright.
segments.buyers: Consumers worldwide, plus fleets and rental firms, sold directly by Tesla (no dealers).
pos: Still the engine: 70% of sales over the last 4 quarters, growing again (+9.6% vs the 4 quarters before; +26.7% in the June quarter vs a year earlier).
Each car is a future customer for FSD subscriptions, Supercharging and insurance (Services).
neg: Not recurring: sold once, and volume swings with prices, incentives and subsidies.

Cheap financing helped 2026 volume and average prices fell. Car sales earn below the company gross margin (see the car-sales margin); in the June quarter the automotive margin excluding credits was 16.3%, up from 15.0% a year earlier but down from Q1's one-off-boosted 19.2%.
Exposed to the China price war, tariffs and memory costs (chains C1, C5).

segments.name: Regulatory credits
segments.sells: Regulatory credits sold to other carmakers that miss emissions or fuel-economy rules.
pos: Almost pure profit when sold: no cost of goods (shown with car sales because Tesla reports their cost together).
neg: Disappearing: −39.8% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before, and $146m in the June quarter vs $439m a year earlier, after US fuel-economy fines were scrapped (chain C4).
Its loss hits gross profit almost one-for-one.

segments.name: Car leasing
segments.sells: Cars leased to customers (Tesla keeps ownership).
segments.buyers: Consumers and businesses that lease rather than buy.
pos: Recurring monthly payments, and leasing has its own, much higher margin than car sales.
neg: Small and shrinking: 1.5% of sales, −11.3% vs the 4 quarters before.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.sells: Services and other: FSD subscriptions, Supercharging, insurance, used cars, repairs, parts and merchandise.
segments.buyers: Tesla owners (and other EV drivers at Superchargers).
pos: Fastest-growing part: +34.0% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before; 14.6% of sales now vs 7.8% three years ago.
Partly recurring (FSD subscriptions, charging, insurance): about 1.5m paying FSD customers at the June quarter, and future FSD sales will mostly be subscriptions.
Margin rising fast: 10.9% (last 4 quarters) vs 5.6% a year earlier.
neg: Still earns below the company gross margin (10.9% vs 18.9%), because used cars and repairs are low-margin.
Robotaxi revenue would land here, but the fleet is still small (about a dozen cars or fewer per city in mid-2026).

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.sells: Battery storage (Megapack for utilities, Powerwall for homes) and solar.
segments.buyers: Utilities, power developers and data centres; homeowners.
pos: Most profitable part: 29.4% gross margin (last 4 quarters) vs 18.9% for the company, up from 13.0% three years ago.
Growing: +16.8% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before; 12.4% of sales vs 5.8% three years ago. Storage deployed +40.6% in the June quarter vs a year earlier.
AI data centres need large batteries, a fresh source of demand.
neg: Lumpy: deployments swing quarter to quarter with big projects.
June-quarter margin dropped to 20.4% after a $240m one-off warranty charge; management expects the low-to-mid 20s % over the long term, below the last-4-quarter 29.4%.
Battery cells are scarce: management named battery capacity a limit (chain C1).

pos: Partly recurring revenue (long-life contracts or design wins) up 8 pts in 3 years to 16% of sales (last 4 quarters).
neg: The shift in mix alone took 0.5 pts off gross margin vs a year earlier (last 4 quarters vs the 4 quarters a year earlier, each part's margin held at that earlier level).
Fastest-growing part (Services and other, +36% vs a year earlier) earns below the company gross margin.
Concentration: Car sales is 70% of sales (last 4 quarters).

shift.title: What the shift means for Tesla
pos: Tesla is slowly becoming less of a pure carmaker: car sales fell from 82% to 70% of revenue in 3 years (last 4 quarters vs the 4 quarters to Jun 2023), while energy rose from 6% to 12% and services from 8% to 15%.
Energy is the profit bright spot: its gross margin rose from 13.0% to 29.4% over the same 3 years, well above the company's 18.9%.
Company gross margin is up from 17.5% to 18.9% (last 4 quarters vs the 4 a year earlier), helped by energy and services margins.
neg: Over 3 years margins fell: derived by difference from SEC figures, the automotive margin was about 23.4% and the company gross margin about 21.5% in the 4 quarters to Jun 2023, vs 18.9% for the company now (the engine shows the 3-year figures as blank, see the note).

The shift is not lifting margins on its own: the mix change alone took about 0.3 points off gross margin vs a year earlier (each part's margin held at that earlier level), because low-margin services grew fastest.
Regulatory credits, almost pure profit, are fading out (1.4% of sales, −39.8% vs the 4 quarters before).
Cars are still 70% of sales, so car pricing and incentives still decide most of the profit.

mix.note: Gross margin by Tesla's own cost lines: car sales and regulatory credits share one cost line (credits have almost no cost), leasing, services and other, and energy each have their own. Margins 3 years ago are blank for car sales, leasing and the company: Tesla's filings before Q3 2022 do not tag these costs, so Q4 2022 cannot be derived (by difference: automotive about 23.4%, company about 21.5%).
